record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Characterize the vertices v of a signed graph Σ that belong only to negative circles, meaning that every circle of Σ containing v is negative.

evidence.quote: V4. In Σ, does vertex v belong only to negative circles? Ans. Conjecture: In every unbalanced block B that contains it, v must be divalent and a balancing vertex (that is, B \ v is balanced).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\Sigma = (G, \sigma)$ consisting of a graph $G = (V, E)$ together with a sign function $\sigma : E \to \{+1, -1\}$. A circle (simple cycle) $C$ in $\Sigma$ is called positive if the product of the signs of its edges equals $+1$, and negative otherwise. The signed graph $\Sigma$ is balanced if every circle of $\Sigma$ is positive. A block of $\Sigma$ is a maximal subgraph having no cut-vertex; a block is unbalanced if it contains at least one negative circle. A vertex $v$ is divalent in a block $B$ if it has exactly two neighbors in $B$. A vertex $v$ is called a balancing vertex of an unbalanced block $B$ if $B \setminus v$ is balanced.

Problem. Characterize all vertices $v$ of a signed graph $\Sigma$ with the property that every circle of $\Sigma$ passing through $v$ is negative. In particular, prove or disprove the following conjectured characterization: $v$ has this property if and only if, in every unbalanced block $B$ of $\Sigma$ that contains $v$, the vertex $v$ is divalent in $B$ and is a balancing vertex of $B$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as a conjecture in Zaslavsky's problem collection on negative circles in signed graphs (originally posted 2016, with a published version in AKCE Int. J. Graphs Comb., 2018). No subsequent paper resolving the conjectured characterization of vertices lying only on negative circles was located, so the problem appears to remain open.
